metadata.title: Machine Base Class
metadata.description: The Machine Base Class (renamed from Compute — ADR-068; the Base test is ADR-069, home docs/spec/foundations/class-tiers.md). A Machine is an OS-bearing execution environment ordered as one deliverable: an image booted onto cpu, memory, disk and network. Its members are the forms that deliverable takes — Machine.VM, Machine.BareMetalHost, Machine.LPAR — and any provider offering one of them can realize an order placed here; OpenStack Nova with Ironic, Cluster API's Machine, and TOSCA's Compute node type are the industry abstractions that already treat them as one thing. Every element here is a SharedDataElement at `Machine` scope, honorable by every form. Containers and Kubernetes clusters are NOT machines: they left this Base because they cannot honor `guest_os` (Container) or carry Kubernetes-only vocabulary (KubernetesCluster).

instance_size.description: Provider-neutral size class (small|medium|large, ordered/comparable — common-elements §2.2, ADR-014). Size by class IN PLACE OF cpu+memory; the provider maps it to concrete resources at naturalization (DCM ADR-023). anyOf enforces sizing by class OR raw.

count.description: Total virtual CPUs. The provider naturalizes this to its native cpu model (a KubeVirt domain cpu, a hypervisor platform's sockets*cores, a public cloud's vCPUs) at realization (DCM ADR-023).

sockets.description: Optional topology hint: sockets. Provider-support-dependent; ignored where not applicable.

cores_per_socket.description: Optional topology hint: cores per socket. Provider-support-dependent.

cpu.description: Unifies vcpu (VM) / cpu (BareMetal) / resources.cpu (Container) — the same concept under three names today. The provider naturalizes to its native model (kubevirt domain cpu, vSphere sockets×cores, EC2 vCPUs).

size.description: Memory allocation, e.g. 16GB or 16Gi (class-aligned quantity pattern — Machine Base Class `memory.size`).

hugepages.description: Optional huge-page backing (provider-support-dependent; validated against provider capability).

memory.description: Reconciles the drift the sweep found (VM had {hugepages,size}, BareMetal had {size}): `hugepages` becomes an optional Base element.

storage.description: The reference-discipline storage requirements descriptor (PVD-001, Machine Base Class shape) — numeric minima the realizing storage must meet. The requested performance class is the governed `storage_tier` element, not an inline enum here.

storage_tier.description: The requested storage performance class — a GOVERNED vocabulary (ADR-038 §2): canonical terms are `storage_tier` reference-data records (standard/performance/archive), each denoting a requirements floor. Name-selectable but requirements-authoritative (ADR-036); profile decides bare string vs data_reference (ADR-007/ADR-039). Mirrors the Machine Base Class `storage_tier` element. Governed vocabulary `storage_tier` (ADR-038 §2); name-selectable but requirements-authoritative (ADR-036). Profile decides bare-vs-reference.

guest_os.description: Guest operating system. Portable form is a reference to an os_image reference-data vocabulary (DCM ADR-012; layering §3.7) the target provider advertises via capability discovery (ADR-PROV-002); policy validates membership at request. Inline is the portability_breaking escape. Optional at the data layer (bare-instantiation philosophy): a VM may be declared by sizing alone; a profile MAY require it.

type.description: Inline OS identifier (e.g. linux-server-9). portability_breaking: a value with no os_image vocabulary entry — a review finding.

provider_handle.description: The provider-native identifier of the realized machine (opaque; correlation and operations only — never a portable reference). Promoted from Machine.VM: every form has one.

primary_ip.description: The primary or management address of the booted machine — the single address most bindings want. Promoted from Machine.VM: a bare-metal host and an LPAR have one once booted.

hostname.description: Realized hostname (FQDN where the realm provides one). Promoted from Machine.VM.

adopts.role: Vendor-neutral compute-system representation spanning physical, virtual and partitioned (Redfish ComputerSystem SystemType: Physical | Virtual | Composed | PhysicallyPartitioned | VirtuallyPartitioned) — the one representative standard for the Machine family, shared by Machine.VM, Machine.BareMetalHost and Machine.LPAR and declared once here. Nova with Ironic, Cluster API's Machine and TOSCA's Compute are the industry abstractions that treat the three forms as one thing (CLS-002 (a)); Redfish is the wire representation adopted. Provider-native realizations are declared on the provider support matrix, not on the substrate type.

context.purpose: Declares an OS-bearing machine — an image booted onto cpu, memory, disk and network — without saying whether it is a VM, a bare-metal host or a logical partition.
context.plain_description: The most portable way to ask for a machine: how big, what image, what storage tier. Placement decides the form (VM, bare metal, LPAR) and the provider; policy fills what the form needs. A producer bound at any of the three forms must accept this order (class-tiers CLS-002 (c)).
use_when: You need a host and do not care whether it is virtual or physical.
A rebuild after loss where the original form is not worth preserving.
not_for: A container (Container) or a Kubernetes cluster (KubernetesCluster) — neither can honor `guest_os`.
When the form matters — order Machine.VM, Machine.BareMetalHost or Machine.LPAR.
works_with: Machine.VM, Machine.BareMetalHost, Machine.LPAR — the forms an order here resolves to.
Storage.Volume and Network.VirtualNetwork — what the realized machine attaches to.
